newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela seeks $50 mln U.S. trade compensation.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seeks $50 mln U.S. trade compensation.

text.p: Venezuela is seeking $50 million compensation from the United States after the World Trade Organisation ruled that the U.S. unfairly discriminated against its gasoline imports, a Venezuelan official said on Tuesday.
The World Trade Organisation ruled in Venezuela and Brazil's favour after these countries complained in 1995 and the U.S. has promised to modify its laws by August 20 this year.

"We assume there will be some compensation," said Luis Giusti, president of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela. "We don't know what weight they will give to each of the factors, but we said at one point that it had an opportunity cost of about $50 million. We will have to wait for the politicians to resolve it."
Giusti recently returned from a trip to the United States, where he met U.S. energy officials.
Venezuela already had an important trading relationship with the United States, Giusti added, with $8.5 billion in exports and $1.5 billion in imports, and he was seeking to strengthen it.
